subject.title: refactor(push-web): move web push store to shared SQLite state DB

question: Should legacy Web Push JSON import be owned by `openclaw doctor --fix`, or may gateway startup automatically import it and fail closed on malformed files?
rationale: Repository policy assigns persistent legacy-state migration to one doctor-owned path, while the recently merged device-pairing migration provides a conflicting startup-import precedent; the resulting gateway availability and operator-recovery contract requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Use Doctor-Owned Migration
options.body: Move import, verification, and archival into the doctor repair path, keep runtime SQLite-only, and provide an actionable startup diagnostic until repair succeeds.

options.title: Approve Startup Fail-Closed
options.body: Keep startup import as an explicit exception, document the outage and recovery contract, and provide real gateway upgrade proof for valid and corrupt legacy stores.

options.title: Pause the Storage Swap
options.body: Leave the JSON runtime unchanged until a shared, maintainer-approved persistent-state migration framework is available.

recommendation.title: Use Doctor-Owned Migration
recommendation.body: Move import, verification, and archival into the doctor repair path, keep runtime SQLite-only, and provide an actionable startup diagnostic until repair succeeds.

likelyOwner.reason: The adjacent device-pairing SQLite migration is the closest merged precedent for this gateway startup and shared-state decision.
